fields.criterionScope: REQ-035 AC-1–12; complete active configuration-aware engineering change goal
fields.expectedResult: AC-1: Controlled capture retains an explicit bounded set of exact native member/relationship revisions, external observation selections, schema/context and declared scope; omissions and legacy captures never imply undeclared topology/content completeness. Stable caller identity and captured original intent recover an identical committed capture after lost response/restart without duplicate creation or silent rebasing; conflicting intent/guards/provenance reject. AC-2: A deterministic read-only comparison binds two immutable configuration identities and all governing policy/state digests. Later live native/evidence changes do not alter that pair comparison; switching either side is explicit. Incompatible subject/project/model/schema/scope and unavailable historical information produce explained comparability/uncertainty or refusal rather than inferred equivalence. AC-3: Native comparison explains added/removed membership, type/key/resource/field differences and version-only changes with exact original/current-selected versions, schemas and provenance. Missing versus null, ordered arrays and nested JSON remain meaningful. Removed-from-configuration is distinct from deleted-from-project, and mutable current liveness is not silently substituted for the selected state. AC-4: Selected relationship topology comparison preserves exact endpoints, type, metadata and contextual-reference role/selector/state changes, including relinking, removed relationships and historical endpoints. Undeclared legacy topology is explicitly unknown, not an empty complete graph; no reachability implies engineering causation or membership. AC-5: Content comparison uses explicitly captured resource/observation identities, availability and hashes/commits; annotation changes and observed-byte changes remain separate. Same hash is not identity merging or byte retention, and document change cannot establish passage change without sufficient selected evidence. Reads perform no observer IO and never replace pinned selections with the latest observation. AC-6: Configuration-bound dependency/applicability analysis explains changed inputs, potentially affected and unaffected declared scope, exact inclusion/exclusion basis and remaining uncertainty. Captured input field/path/direct-link/content semantics are reused; incomplete scope, absent evidence and unknown availability cannot establish no impact. Bounded populations and summaries state completeness and refuse overflow explicitly. AC-7: Controlled pair-bound assessments preserve the original pair/policy and every discovered obligation, reasoned disposition, action and immutable conclusion. No-action, investigation, required revision and re-verification remain distinct. Pair/policy changes require explicit reassessment while retaining prior judgments; closure requires complete accounting under the pinned policy and never implies release approval. AC-8: Verification follow-through retains exact criterion/method/candidate/support states and explains whether selected recorded outcomes apply to the target configuration, independently of unrelated live-head changes. Existing current-head verification keeps its meaning. Failed/not_run results stay non-passing; generic reviews/status strings cannot override changed governing criteria, incomplete accounting or unknown support. Work executed after configuration capture can support that candidate only through validated exact input correspondence and explicit provenance, never by silently adding membership. AC-9: Core, typed HTTP/client and CLI/agent interfaces share the same domain operations, captured queries and original-intent recovery. Atomic guards reject stale/concurrent/invalid proposals without partial state/history/evidence/outcomes; failed reads pause writes and uncertain writes are inspected without automatic replay. Existing API/storage/receipt/configuration/baseline/assessment/verification contracts retain their semantics and historical readability. AC-10: The shared workspace captures/selects the pair, explains native/content/topology differences and comparable/unknown scope, investigates consequences, records dispositions, opens appropriate existing assessment/verification follow-through and shows outstanding/resolved work. Drafts survive navigation, stale inputs require explicit adoption, lost responses use shared recovery and supported responsive views preserve exact context. A fresh independent agent completes an unfamiliar task and material findings are addressed; human validation remains separate. AC-11: A justified real Tracer software change retains exact before/after configurations and original conclusions, identifies actual changed and unaffected scope, completes necessary assessment/verification and explains final remaining work without manufactured engineering claims. A materially different configured domain demonstrates the same semantics. Exact candidate/procedure/results cover additions/removals, reference/content changes, unavailable/deleted inputs, partial/incompatible scope, drift, supersession/reassessment and workload/payload boundaries. AC-12: Existing identities, native/evidence history, command outcomes and both prior application capabilities are preserved; necessary migrations are rehearsed and deterministic export/online SQLite backup/restored recovery verified. Appropriate regression, browser, architecture and quality gates pass unchanged. Owning architecture/usage docs, checkpoint and register retain exact evidence, unchanged criteria, delivery/verification/human-validation distinctions and remaining limits. Full goal acceptance is audited before completion.
fields.method: Use projects/tracer/configuration-change-specification.json and the owning architecture contracts. Verify immutable native/content/topology capture and exact recovery, two-configuration comparison independent of live head, comparability/partial/unknown bounds, pair-bound assessment and target-configuration verification. Exercise core/HTTP/CLI and shared UI through success, rejection, concurrency, stale reads, lost responses, deleted history, reassessment and limits. Run the justified actual Tracer capture enhancement and second configured domain, fresh-agent comprehension with findings addressed, full unchanged quality/migration/compatibility and live/export/restored-backup preservation. Audit all twelve criteria and the complete goal before promotion.

criteria.quote: AC-1: Controlled capture retains an explicit bounded set of exact native member/relationship revisions, external observation selections, schema/context and declared scope; omissions and legacy captures never imply undeclared topology/content completeness. Stable caller identity and captured original intent recover an identical committed capture after lost response/restart without duplicate creation or silent rebasing; conflicting intent/guards/provenance reject.

AC-2: A deterministic read-only comparison binds two immutable configuration identities and all governing policy/state digests. Later live native/evidence changes do not alter that pair comparison; switching either side is explicit. Incompatible subject/project/model/schema/scope and unavailable historical information produce explained comparability/uncertainty or refusal rather than inferred equivalence.

AC-3: Native comparison explains added/removed membership, type/key/resource/field differences and version-only changes with exact original/current-selected versions, schemas and provenance. Missing versus null, ordered arrays and nested JSON remain meaningful. Removed-from-configuration is distinct from deleted-from-project, and mutable current liveness is not silently substituted for the selected state.

AC-4: Selected relationship topology comparison preserves exact endpoints, type, metadata and contextual-reference role/selector/state changes, including relinking, removed relationships and historical endpoints. Undeclared legacy topology is explicitly unknown, not an empty complete graph; no reachability implies engineering causation or membership.

AC-5: Content comparison uses explicitly captured resource/observation identities, availability and hashes/commits; annotation changes and observed-byte changes remain separate. Same hash is not identity merging or byte retention, and document change cannot establish passage change without sufficient selected evidence. Reads perform no observer IO and never replace pinned selections with the latest observation.

AC-6: Configuration-bound dependency/applicability analysis explains changed inputs, potentially affected and unaffected declared scope, exact inclusion/exclusion basis and remaining uncertainty. Captured input field/path/direct-link/content semantics are reused; incomplete scope, absent evidence and unknown availability cannot establish no impact. Bounded populations and summaries state completeness and refuse overflow explicitly.

AC-7: Controlled pair-bound assessments preserve the original pair/policy and every discovered obligation, reasoned disposition, action and immutable conclusion. No-action, investigation, required revision and re-verification remain distinct. Pair/policy changes require explicit reassessment while retaining prior judgments; closure requires complete accounting under the pinned policy and never implies release approval.

AC-8: Verification follow-through retains exact criterion/method/candidate/support states and explains whether selected recorded outcomes apply to the target configuration, independently of unrelated live-head changes. Existing current-head verification keeps its meaning. Failed/not_run results stay non-passing; generic reviews/status strings cannot override changed governing criteria, incomplete accounting or unknown support. Work executed after configuration capture can support that candidate only through validated exact input correspondence and explicit provenance, never by silently adding membership.

AC-9: Core, typed HTTP/client and CLI/agent interfaces share the same domain operations, captured queries and original-intent recovery. Atomic guards reject stale/concurrent/invalid proposals without partial state/history/evidence/outcomes; failed reads pause writes and uncertain writes are inspected without automatic replay. Existing API/storage/receipt/configuration/baseline/assessment/verification contracts retain their semantics and historical readability.

AC-10: The shared workspace captures/selects the pair, explains native/content/topology differences and comparable/unknown scope, investigates consequences, records dispositions, opens appropriate existing assessment/verification follow-through and shows outstanding/resolved work. Drafts survive navigation, stale inputs require explicit adoption, lost responses use shared recovery and supported responsive views preserve exact context. A fresh independent agent completes an unfamiliar task and material findings are addressed; human validation remains separate.

AC-11: A justified real Tracer software change retains exact before/after configurations and original conclusions, identifies actual changed and unaffected scope, completes necessary assessment/verification and explains final remaining work without manufactured engineering claims. A materially different configured domain demonstrates the same semantics. Exact candidate/procedure/results cover additions/removals, reference/content changes, unavailable/deleted inputs, partial/incompatible scope, drift, supersession/reassessment and workload/payload boundaries.

AC-12: Existing identities, native/evidence history, command outcomes and both prior application capabilities are preserved; necessary migrations are rehearsed and deterministic export/online SQLite backup/restored recovery verified. Appropriate regression, browser, architecture and quality gates pass unchanged. Owning architecture/usage docs, checkpoint and register retain exact evidence, unchanged criteria, delivery/verification/human-validation distinctions and remaining limits. Full goal acceptance is audited before completion.

criteria.quote: AC-1: Controlled capture retains an explicit bounded set of exact native member/relationship revisions, external observation selections, schema/context and declared scope; omissions and legacy captures never imply undeclared topology/content completeness. Stable caller identity and captured original intent recover an identical committed capture after lost response/restart without duplicate creation or silent rebasing; conflicting intent/guards/provenance reject.

AC-2: A deterministic read-only comparison binds two immutable configuration identities and all governing policy/state digests. Later live native/evidence changes do not alter that pair comparison; switching either side is explicit. Incompatible subject/project/model/schema/scope and unavailable historical information produce explained comparability/uncertainty or refusal rather than inferred equivalence.

AC-3: Native comparison explains added/removed membership, type/key/resource/field differences and version-only changes with exact original/current-selected versions, schemas and provenance. Missing versus null, ordered arrays and nested JSON remain meaningful. Removed-from-configuration is distinct from deleted-from-project, and mutable current liveness is not silently substituted for the selected state.

AC-4: Selected relationship topology comparison preserves exact endpoints, type, metadata and contextual-reference role/selector/state changes, including relinking, removed relationships and historical endpoints. Undeclared legacy topology is explicitly unknown, not an empty complete graph; no reachability implies engineering causation or membership.

AC-5: Content comparison uses explicitly captured resource/observation identities, availability and hashes/commits; annotation changes and observed-byte changes remain separate. Same hash is not identity merging or byte retention, and document change cannot establish passage change without sufficient selected evidence. Reads perform no observer IO and never replace pinned selections with the latest observation.

AC-6: Configuration-bound dependency/applicability analysis explains changed inputs, potentially affected and unaffected declared scope, exact inclusion/exclusion basis and remaining uncertainty. Captured input field/path/direct-link/content semantics are reused; incomplete scope, absent evidence and unknown availability cannot establish no impact. Bounded populations and summaries state completeness and refuse overflow explicitly.

AC-7: Controlled pair-bound assessments preserve the original pair/policy and every discovered obligation, reasoned disposition, action and immutable conclusion. No-action, investigation, required revision and re-verification remain distinct. Pair/policy changes require explicit reassessment while retaining prior judgments; closure requires complete accounting under the pinned policy and never implies release approval.

AC-8: Verification follow-through retains exact criterion/method/candidate/support states and explains whether selected recorded outcomes apply to the target configuration, independently of unrelated live-head changes. Existing current-head verification keeps its meaning. Failed/not_run results stay non-passing; generic reviews/status strings cannot override changed governing criteria, incomplete accounting or unknown support. Work executed after configuration capture can support that candidate only through validated exact input correspondence and explicit provenance, never by silently adding membership.

AC-9: Core, typed HTTP/client and CLI/agent interfaces share the same domain operations, captured queries and original-intent recovery. Atomic guards reject stale/concurrent/invalid proposals without partial state/history/evidence/outcomes; failed reads pause writes and uncertain writes are inspected without automatic replay. Existing API/storage/receipt/configuration/baseline/assessment/verification contracts retain their semantics and historical readability.

AC-10: The shared workspace captures/selects the pair, explains native/content/topology differences and comparable/unknown scope, investigates consequences, records dispositions, opens appropriate existing assessment/verification follow-through and shows outstanding/resolved work. Drafts survive navigation, stale inputs require explicit adoption, lost responses use shared recovery and supported responsive views preserve exact context. A fresh independent agent completes an unfamiliar task and material findings are addressed; human validation remains separate.

AC-11: A justified real Tracer software change retains exact before/after configurations and original conclusions, identifies actual changed and unaffected scope, completes necessary assessment/verification and explains final remaining work without manufactured engineering claims. A materially different configured domain demonstrates the same semantics. Exact candidate/procedure/results cover additions/removals, reference/content changes, unavailable/deleted inputs, partial/incompatible scope, drift, supersession/reassessment and workload/payload boundaries.

AC-12: Existing identities, native/evidence history, command outcomes and both prior application capabilities are preserved; necessary migrations are rehearsed and deterministic export/online SQLite backup/restored recovery verified. Appropriate regression, browser, architecture and quality gates pass unchanged. Owning architecture/usage docs, checkpoint and register retain exact evidence, unchanged criteria, delivery/verification/human-validation distinctions and remaining limits. Full goal acceptance is audited before completion.

fields.expectedResult: AC-1: Controlled capture retains an explicit bounded set of exact native member/relationship revisions, external observation selections, schema/context and declared scope; omissions and legacy captures never imply undeclared topology/content completeness. Stable caller identity and captured original intent recover an identical committed capture after lost response/restart without duplicate creation or silent rebasing; conflicting intent/guards/provenance reject. AC-2: A deterministic read-only comparison binds two immutable configuration identities and all governing policy/state digests. Later live native/evidence changes do not alter that pair comparison; switching either side is explicit. Incompatible subject/project/model/schema/scope and unavailable historical information produce explained comparability/uncertainty or refusal rather than inferred equivalence. AC-3: Native comparison explains added/removed membership, type/key/resource/field differences and version-only changes with exact original/current-selected versions, schemas and provenance. Missing versus null, ordered arrays and nested JSON remain meaningful. Removed-from-configuration is distinct from deleted-from-project, and mutable current liveness is not silently substituted for the selected state. AC-4: Selected relationship topology comparison preserves exact endpoints, type, metadata and contextual-reference role/selector/state changes, including relinking, removed relationships and historical endpoints. Undeclared legacy topology is explicitly unknown, not an empty complete graph; no reachability implies engineering causation or membership. AC-5: Content comparison uses explicitly captured resource/observation identities, availability and hashes/commits; annotation changes and observed-byte changes remain separate. Same hash is not identity merging or byte retention, and document change cannot establish passage change without sufficient selected evidence. Reads perform no observer IO and never replace pinned selections with the latest observation. AC-6: Configuration-bound dependency/applicability analysis explains changed inputs, potentially affected and unaffected declared scope, exact inclusion/exclusion basis and remaining uncertainty. Captured input field/path/direct-link/content semantics are reused; incomplete scope, absent evidence and unknown availability cannot establish no impact. Bounded populations and summaries state completeness and refuse overflow explicitly. AC-7: Controlled pair-bound assessments preserve the original pair/policy and every discovered obligation, reasoned disposition, action and immutable conclusion. No-action, investigation, required revision and re-verification remain distinct. Pair/policy changes require explicit reassessment while retaining prior judgments; closure requires complete accounting under the pinned policy and never implies release approval. AC-8: Verification follow-through retains exact criterion/method/candidate/support states and explains whether selected recorded outcomes apply to the target configuration, independently of unrelated live-head changes. Existing current-head verification keeps its meaning. Failed/not_run results stay non-passing; generic reviews/status strings cannot override changed governing criteria, incomplete accounting or unknown support. Work executed after configuration capture can support that candidate only through validated exact input correspondence and explicit provenance, never by silently adding membership. AC-9: Core, typed HTTP/client and CLI/agent interfaces share the same domain operations, captured queries and original-intent recovery. Atomic guards reject stale/concurrent/invalid proposals without partial state/history/evidence/outcomes; failed reads pause writes and uncertain writes are inspected without automatic replay. AC-10: The shared workspace captures/selects the pair, explains native/content/topology differences and comparable/unknown scope, investigates consequences, records dispositions, opens appropriate existing assessment/verification follow-through and shows outstanding/resolved work. Owning architecture/usage docs, checkpoint and register retain exact evidence, unchanged criteria, delivery/verification/human-validation distinctions and remaining limits. acceptance.acceptance: AC-1: Controlled capture retains an explicit bounded set of exact native member/relationship revisions, external observation selections, schema/context and declared scope; omissions and legacy captures never imply undeclared topology/content completeness. Stable caller identity and captured original intent recover an identical committed capture after lost response/restart without duplicate creation or silent rebasing; conflicting intent/guards/provenance reject. AC-2: A deterministic read-only comparison binds two immutable configuration identities and all governing policy/state digests. Later live native/evidence changes do not alter that pair comparison; switching either side is explicit. Incompatible subject/project/model/schema/scope and unavailable historical information produce explained comparability/uncertainty or refusal rather than inferred equivalence. AC-3: Native comparison explains added/removed membership, type/key/resource/field differences and version-only changes with exact original/current-selected versions, schemas and provenance. Missing versus null, ordered arrays and nested JSON remain meaningful. Removed-from-configuration is distinct from deleted-from-project, and mutable current liveness is not silently substituted for the selected state. AC-4: Selected relationship topology comparison preserves exact endpoints, type, metadata and contextual-reference role/selector/state changes, including relinking, removed relationships and historical endpoints. Undeclared legacy topology is explicitly unknown, not an empty complete graph; no reachability implies engineering causation or membership. AC-5: Content comparison uses explicitly captured resource/observation identities, availability and hashes/commits; annotation changes and observed-byte changes remain separate. Same hash is not identity merging or byte retention, and document change cannot establish passage change without sufficient selected evidence. Reads perform no observer IO and never replace pinned selections with the latest observation. AC-6: Configuration-bound dependency/applicability analysis explains changed inputs, potentially affected and unaffected declared scope, exact inclusion/exclusion basis and remaining uncertainty. AC-7: Controlled pair-bound assessments preserve the original pair/policy and every discovered obligation, reasoned disposition, action and immutable conclusion. fields.acceptance: AC-1: Independent repository handles and OS processes preserve unique identities, stale object/schema/project/endpoint guards, atomic rollback, ordered immutable history and usable recovery across concurrent native/schema/link/resource operations. Every acknowledged update survives; contention may reject explicitly without silent replay. AC-2: Identical and conflicting command IDs under genuine process overlap produce at most one durable success per family/identity with exact original intent/outcome inspection after reopen; native plus receipt changes never publish partially. AC-3: Declared read-only operations observe one committed native/evidence snapshot without reserving the writer slot. Readers coexist with readers and an active writer under WAL; writes through a read-only transaction reject atomically. Separate requests retain their existing pagination guarantees, without an invented shared snapshot; guarded continuations reject changes as already promised. AC-4: Genuinely concurrent assessment and verification work preserves pinned models, selected configuration comparison and candidate applicability. Unrelated head changes never silently change fixed pair meaning; conflicting basis, actions or conclusions reject or require deliberate reassessment. AC-5: Process termination before commit leaves no partial native/evidence/outcome writes; termination after commit and response loss recovers exact original success by inspection after restart. No automatic uncertain-write replay. AC-6: SQLite-aware online backup during active work restores a complete committed state with native/evidence history and outcome identities intact; current engineering application capabilities remain usable after restore. AC-7: Reproducible real-project and connected synthetic workloads report exact candidate, environment, counts, latency distributions, RSS/heap, payload/work bounds and contention. Explicit engineering budgets are fixed after initial baseline and before optimization; overflow is explained, never silently truncated. AC-8: Core, typed HTTP/client, CLI and relevant existing shared-workspace task checks cover success, rejection and uncertain recovery under declared workloads. Portable contracts distinguish adapter obligations from SQLite implementation proof; future authentication/backend parity stays unproven. AC-9: Appropriate unchanged regression, browser, architecture and quality checks pass. Owning docs, checkpoint, guarded register, deterministic export and restored online backup retain exact evidence, limits and independent delivery/verification/human-validation status. Audit all criteria and the complete goal before completion.

fields.excerpt:
## Product vision

**Status:** owner-authored direction from the initial brief; not representative-user evidence or implementation approval.

Make structured engineering information as easy to create, connect and edit as a spreadsheet, with typed relationships, traceability, history and meaningful change context. The owner's experience of navigation and process overhead in enterprise requirements tools motivates this hypothesis.

Use one domain-independent model for humans and agents. Begin locally with a project database, minimal setup and no cloud account. Deeper traceability and team use should grow from the same semantics without complicating ordinary authoring. Shared servers, PostgreSQL, permissions and broad collaboration remain future work.

The original need IDs remain stable:

### UN-001 — Organize structured information

Configure familiar information types—requirements, designs, components, tests, risks, decisions, tasks, experiments and evidence—without changing Tracer's source. Templates are optional; a task tracker should not require requirements-management vocabulary.

### UN-002 — Connect information

Create typed, directed relationships with their own identity, fields and history. Navigate in either direction across hierarchies, shared contributions and cross-domain networks without forcing a tree.

### UN-003 — Understand completeness and impact

Find gaps and possible change consequences under explicit project expectations. Reachability, structural completeness, assessed impact and successful execution are distinct; links and coverage counts do not establish satisfaction or readiness.

### UN-004 — Track changes and preserve history

Explain what changed, when, why and by whom, including relationships. Reconstruct reproducible baselines and compare logical states through semantic and deterministic textual differences. Full export/diff/restoration workflows remain undelivered.

### UN-005 — Work through the most appropriate interface

Use tables, graphs, matrices or document-like views over the same information, validation and history. The selected map experience is shared across examples. This goal does not imply every view currently supports every edit.

### Scope, generality and limits

Medical devices, software, aerospace, manufacturing/quality, research and regulatory evidence use the same primitives and may coexist in one project. Optional schemas express vocabulary and policy; they neither establish compliance nor impose universal approval stages. See [industry workflows](industry-workflows/README.md).

Start with a useful local engineering foundation. Enterprise requirements-tool parity, PLM/ERP, specialized compliance, distributed storage, comprehensive workflow automation and an elaborate plugin ecosystem are outside initial scope. Add infrastructure when its value is demonstrated.

[Vision scenarios](user-journeys.md#vision-scenarios-and-remaining-proof) make the ambition testable; [validation milestones](development-flow.md#validation-milestones) define the required evidence.

fields.excerpt:
## 5. Small readiness/completion decisions

- **Ready to implement:** selected task/concept, bounded scope, sufficient evidence, failure handling, checks and validation plan. Experiment on risky unknowns.
- **Implemented/verified:** agreed behavior passes checks; candidate and limits are reviewable.
- **Validated:** representative task evidence supports a stated use/context. Owner walkthroughs remain provisional.
- **Release-ready:** appropriate usefulness, correctness and operational evidence, resolved critical dependencies and explicit authority.

After sustaining changes, reassess affected specs, checks and scenarios. Retain passing evidence where its coverage remains applicable.

fields.excerpt:
## Current limits

- The production map reads a transactional native snapshot bounded to 10,000 artifacts and 100,000 relationships. Drawing/query bounds are disclosed separately.
- The workbench draws up to 50 artifacts and projects up to 500 trace rows or 100 terminal links per grouped cell. It is not virtualized.
- Assessment discovery follows declared input/captured-output scope, five evaluations per page. Ordinary graph connectivity is not an assessed dependency or proof of impact.
- Unsaved drafts remain tab-local and are deliberately excluded from recovery. Leaving/reloading warns; uncertain writes restore a pause without replay. Spatial and investigation recovery uses browser local storage, keyed by project identity and tied to the same browser/origin. Saved engineering records, review decisions and named Matrix path recipes persist in SQLite.
- Spreadsheet paste/bulk mutation, portable workspace context and arbitrary two-revision comparison remain open. Matrix saved recipes currently support outgoing path columns; receipt creation pickers remain bounded to 1,000 items.
- PostgreSQL parity, authenticated collaboration, hosted integrations, restoration and standalone packaging remain future work.

fields.excerpt:
## Open work

Evaluate complete create → connect → modify → investigate → assess tasks with representative users in more than one domain. An unfamiliar-user session has not been run. Use observed next-action choices, completion time, assistance, errors and context loss to prioritize larger-dataset interaction, clearer review context and remaining authoring friction. Automated checks and visual consistency are supporting evidence, not substitutes for task validation.

fields.statement: Work with parents, children, siblings and cross-cutting relationships together; explain contributions, navigate whole/detail and recognize shared identity. **Basis:** UR-1/2/4/7/14; VI-1. Investigate direction, multiple parents, link attributes, dense branches and branch-level actions. Software may connect needs, modules and tests without successive requirement levels; no strict tree is required. The Jama criticism is owner experience, not a claim about every version.
fields.title: Understand and manipulate relationships across levels

fields.sourceHeading: ### PN-04 — Identify meaningful completeness gaps and next work
fields.statement: Explain an unresolved obligation under declared project expectations and choose the next action. **Basis:** UR-4/15; VI-1. An approved requirement lacking an implementation link is a candidate gap: code may exist but be unlinked. Planned, partial, outdated and current realization must remain distinguishable, including relevant requirement/version scope. Approval, implementation coverage, test coverage and execution results are separate. Investigate applicability and priority; automatic scheduling/ownership remain HY.
fields.title: Identify meaningful completeness gaps and next work

fields.sourceHeading: ### PN-05 — Understand a proposed change before committing it
fields.statement: Start from one modification/removal, compare intent and see candidate consequences with recorded paths or stated reasoning. Retain system requirements whether preserved or explicitly revised. **Basis:** UR-4/6/11/14; VI-1. Motor/load/timing examples are user reports without supplied design/test artifacts. Investigate proposal staging, review, removal, old evidence and unaffected links; no impact algorithm or approval workflow is selected. Missing paths cannot prove no impact.
fields.title: Understand a proposed change before committing it

fields.sourceHeading: ### PN-06 — Track important quantitative meaning without forcing formalization
fields.statement: Explain limits, allocations and derivations while preserving prose and judgment. Avoid coupling identical numbers or silently rewriting children. **Basis:** UR-5; structured parameters/computation are HY; no real quantitative artifact yet. Investigate references, inheritance, budgets, formulas, independent choices, units, overhead, uncertainty and conditions. Formula editing and extraction are not requirements.

fields.statement: Inspect relevant inputs/evidence, understand changed or unknown conditions and retain reasoning. **Basis:** VI-1, existing evidence semantics, UR-14; detailed reviewer tasks are HY. Investigate review packages, comparisons, handoffs and authority. A test file, code link and revision-specific result are separate facts; none alone proves need satisfaction. Local review does not imply organizational or medical sign-off.
fields.title: Judge evidence and record a defensible decision

fields.sourceHeading: ### PN-08 — Trust history and recover safely
fields.statement: Know what changed/saved, preserve attempted proposals and reconcile interruptions or conflicts without silent loss. Distinguish current, draft and historical information. **Basis:** VI-1, UR-2; preferred recovery is HY. Investigate undo scope, autosave, offline work, interruptions and restoration; history is not undo.
fields.title: Trust history and recover safely

fields.statement: Retain scope, selection, drafts and a return path across overview, branch, item and evidence work. **Basis:** UR-1–3/7–8/33/37; VI-1. Investigate persistent state, simultaneous context, keyboard/accessibility, narrow layouts, categorization and direct/contextual actions. Tabs, panels and styling are solutions to evaluate.

fields.statement:
### ND-01 — begin without an extensive setup detour

> As an author starting a design, I want to work with recognizable information so I can begin expressing the design instead of learning the tool's internal model.

**Needs:** PN-01, PN-02. **Basis:** vision plus hypothesis; preferred onboarding method unknown.

**Candidate acceptance:** users recognize the available information and what is missing; they can start one meaningful item without first constructing a complete project ontology. Existing data brought into the project is not silently lost or falsely represented as validated.

**Investigate:** write from scratch, paste/import or start from a template? Prototype these alternatives rather than implementing all three now.
fields.title: begin without an extensive setup detour

fields.sourceHeading: ### ND-02 — author in context and move between levels
fields.statement:
### ND-02 — author in context and move between levels

> As an author, I want to inspect the relevant parent intent while writing a child requirement so I can explain how the child contributes without repeatedly reconstructing context.

**Needs:** PN-02, PN-03, PN-09. **Basis:** UR-1, UR-2, UR-4.

**Candidate acceptance:** free text is usable without compulsory formal syntax; an item can relate to an existing parent or remain explicitly unlinked; applicable field/relationship actions are reachable in the working context; changing scope does not silently lose the draft.

**Exceptions:** long statements, optional attributes, multiple parents, uncertain relationships and a parent that changed while drafting.
fields.title: author in context and move between levels

fields.sourceHeading: ### ND-03 — inspect siblings and shared identity
fields.statement:
### ND-03 — inspect siblings and shared identity

> As an engineer reviewing decomposition, I want to see the other items contributing under the relevant parent so I can judge the family together rather than inspect isolated statements.

**Needs:** PN-03, PN-09. **Basis:** UR-1.

**Candidate acceptance:** the parent and relationship defining the family are explainable; shared children remain recognizable as the same underlying item; editing one identity does not create divergence among its appearances; users can return to the wider scope with drafts intact.

**Exceptions:** a child belongs to two parents, appears along several paths, or has different kinds of sibling relationships. Test whether the user wants immediate siblings or the whole branch; do not assume they are equivalent.
fields.title: inspect siblings and shared identity

fields.sourceHeading: ### ND-04 — resolve one meaningful completeness gap
fields.statement:
### ND-04 — resolve one meaningful completeness gap

> As an engineer building a design, I want to know which obligation is unresolved and why so I can choose the next appropriate work.

**Needs:** PN-04, PN-03, PN-07. **Basis:** UR-4, UR-15; exact scope/policies are HY.

**Candidate acceptance:** a displayed gap has an explainable expectation and scope; the user can inspect existing candidates before creating duplicate information; an appropriate new connection resolves that structural gap without falsely declaring the design/evidence valid; other unresolved obligations remain visible.

**Software acceptance example (UR-15):** where the project marks a requirement approved, see whether an actual implementation artifact is linked. With no such link, show implementation as not traced and likely outstanding; offer the task choices of implementing it, linking existing code or investigating uncertainty. Do not force a new implementation when the code already exists. A link to a planned task/design is not an actual-code realization link; partial or outdated mappings retain their unresolved scope. Adding an appropriate link closes the trace gap, not automatically the implementation/verification judgment.

**Exceptions:** an item is intentionally not applicable, the expectation is unknown, existing implementation is unlinked, a link covers only part of the requirement or refers to older behavior, or old evidence uses different inputs. Represent uncertainty rather than inventing a complete/incomplete judgment.
fields.title: resolve one meaningful completeness gap

fields.sourceHeading: ### SC-01 — see impact before accepting a change
fields.statement:
### SC-01 — see impact before accepting a change

> As an engineer proposing a modification, I want to compare it with the established state and inspect explainable consequences so I can review the proposal before changing the authoritative design.

**Needs:** PN-05, PN-03, PN-08. **Basis:** UR-4, UR-6, UR-11; specific staging mechanisms are HY.

**Candidate acceptance:** proposed versus committed information is distinguishable; impact candidates show the paths/reasons that make them relevant; browsing does not write changes; connection alone is not presented as proof that the connected item must change; unmodeled consequences remain explicitly possible.

**Exceptions:** cyclic or dense networks, shared children, changed schema, missing/deleted items and incomplete source knowledge. A bounded result must explain its scope, not imply a complete impact census.
fields.title: see impact before accepting a change

fields.sourceHeading: ### SC-02 — reason about removal
fields.statement:
### SC-02 — reason about removal

> As an engineer considering removing information, I want to see what relies on it so I can decide how to address those obligations without losing the established history.

**Needs:** PN-05, PN-03, PN-08. **Basis:** UR-4.

**Candidate acceptance:** removing, filtering out, disconnecting and superseding are distinguishable; references and unresolved obligations are explained; no silent cascade; established history remains inspectable; users know whether anything was committed.

**Investigate:** actual review/approval authority and the semantics of retirement versus deletion. Do not introduce automatic cascade or organizational approval merely because it would simplify a mockup.
fields.title: reason about removal

fields.sourceHeading: ### SC-03 — reassess evidence without rewriting its past
fields.statement:
### SC-03 — reassess evidence without rewriting its past

> As a reviewer, I want to inspect changed inputs and the original evidence so I can record why the evidence does or does not support the decision now.

**Needs:** PN-07, PN-05, PN-08. **Basis:** vision/existing evidence model; detailed reviewer task is HY.

**Candidate acceptance:** coverage, freshness, uncertainty and review decision remain separate; original snapshots/rationale remain accessible; the comparison used while drafting is identifiable; a relevant intervening change requires an explicit new assessment rather than silent token adoption; acceptance does not erase drift.

**Exceptions:** missing observations, unrelated edits, relevant later changes, superseded evidence and conflicting reviewer assumptions. Local provenance labels are not authenticated approval authority.
fields.title: reassess evidence without rewriting its past

fields.sourceHeading: ## 4. Cross-cutting story Q-01 — quantitative meaning without overconstraint
fields.statement:
## 4. Cross-cutting story Q-01 — quantitative meaning without overconstraint

> As an engineer changing an important specification, I want to understand where the value comes from and where it is used so I can assess the consequences without forcing every requirement into a formal model.

**Needs:** PN-06, PN-02, PN-05. **Basis:** UR-5; representation and computation are HY.

**Toy scenario:** an overall timing limit is 100 ms, with explicitly declared 60 ms and 40 ms allocations. Propose changing the total to 80 ms. These are not medical specifications. Any arithmetic requires explicit combination and overhead assumptions.

**Candidate acceptance examples:**

- Free-text-only requirements remain authorable and reviewable.
- If a value is deliberately shared, its confirmed consumers are identifiable; an unrelated identical number is not automatically coupled.
- An explicitly modeled calculation may report a result/violation under its declared assumptions, with units and explanation.
- A parent limit change exposes the allocation question but does not silently proportionally scale or rewrite children.
- A child allocation change can raise a feasibility question for the parent without rewriting the parent's intent.
- Missing derivation knowledge is not represented as a satisfied constraint or no impact.
- Declared constraints, possible engineering impact and review decisions are distinguishable.

**Alternatives to test:** ordinary prose with annotated values, optional named typed values, linked value references, and human-authored derivation explanations. A general formula language or extraction engine is not assumed.

**Additional cases:** inconsistent units, rounding, tolerances, ranges, conditions, repeated values, independent choices and removal of a referenced value. Replace the toy example with one real artifact before specifying storage or arithmetic behavior.
fields.title: quantitative meaning without overconstraint

fields.sourceHeading: ## 5. Cross-cutting story R-01 — resume and recover safely
fields.statement:
## 5. Cross-cutting story R-01 — resume and recover safely

> As an engineer interrupted during work, I want to retain my proposal and orientation so I can resume or reconcile it without losing information or overwriting someone else's change.

**Needs:** PN-08, PN-09. **Basis:** vision; preferred saving/recovery model is HY.

**Candidate acceptance:** context/selection and save status are understandable; switching level or representation does not silently discard drafts; a failed read cannot authorize editing stale information as if current; object/schema conflicts preserve the attempt; historical inspection does not masquerade as editing current state.

**Investigate:** autosave versus explicit save, reopening after shutdown, undo, and what should be retained across sessions. Prototype and actual repository safety capabilities may differ; label unsupported recovery behavior honestly.
fields.title: resume and recover safely

## Practical CSV import

2026-10-17: [UR-60](user-needs.md) adds **Project tools → Import CSV** with file/paste input, schema-aware column mapping, optional outgoing links and a separate existing-record link mode. Exact case-sensitive active keys resolve existing records and later rows in the same file. Duplicate keys/connections, malformed rows, missing targets, invalid endpoints and required/typed cell errors block the entire import; ignored columns are explicit. Preview rows/errors page locally without truncating validation. CSV drafts remain tab-local.

The portable parser/planner exports feed the existing guarded changeset route; there is no staging store, alternate write path or storage migration. Explicit create IDs, model/endpoint captures and duplicate-link guards preserve native validation and unknown-outcome inspection. Optional native changeset `expectedProjectRevision` is checked inside the transaction before writes; CSV commits supply the exact preview head, so any intervening native change requires a new preview. Preview also rejects files whose resulting counts would exceed the shared complete-workspace bounds. Confirmed saves identify one revision and clear the draft; failed/uncertain saves retain data/mapping without replay or partial records/history.

The final `npm run check` passed formatting, strict types, lint, 391 unit tests, 144 browser tests, production/harness builds, all workbench journeys and dependency/duplication/complexity gates. Eleven CSV unit cases cover quoting/physical lines, typed values, forward/existing keys, duplicate and missing links, mapping/batch/byte/population limits, captured-head checks, stale endpoints/schema and full rollback. Four browser journeys cover desktop/680px mapping/error/commit/read-back/reload, stale-preview rejection and lost-response locking. Additional browser checks verified malformed UTF-8/CSV, complete error/row pagination and successful link-only import with metadata. Preview/error screenshots were inspected at both widths; 140 local file/heading links resolved. The full run also caught and corrected the retained desk-light journey's old documentation path; it now reads the customization guide. No quality limits or exclusions changed.

One file imports one record type or one relationship type; record mode can add up to eight outgoing key-column link mappings. Existing records are never overwritten. Workbook parsing, updates/merges, saved mapping recipes, multi-key cells and evidence/file import remain outside this slice. The [CSV import guide](csv-import.md) owns formats, bounds and the reusable script workflow.

Shared query codecs fix the impact relationship-type array mismatch. Strict request objects reject unsupported fields, including actor/provenance injection; schema/session reads now reject query parameters. Shared error codes feed client decoding and exhaustive HTTP status mapping.

Added the separate `@tracer-local/core/client` source entry point and routed browser adapters through it without bypassing the mutation controller. Readiness for organizational hosting and PostgreSQL parity remain separate future work. The architecture and developer reference own the contracts, usage and recovery guidance.

Strict validation exposed the shared object editor sending stored relationship `id`/`version` metadata inside an update's `input`. It now constructs the declared type/source/target/fields payload, keeping identity/version guards at operation level. ## Durable changeset command recovery

2026-10-18: added optional project-scoped `commandId` to changeset input and `Tracer.getChangesetOutcome`, with shared HTTP/client and CLI access. Commands retain invocation-time input/provenance, compare canonical intent before current-state guards, and return the original committed result for an exact repeat. Different content, guards, operation order or trusted provenance under a successful identity conflict. Unidentified calls preserve their existing behavior. Result types moved to core with their public application re-exports retained.

Application-owned transaction operations persist successful outcomes atomically with native state, history and revision allocation. SQLite physical format 9 adds immutable outcomes with unique command/changeset identities; older-format migrations preserve existing data/history. Rejections and rollbacks reserve no command ID. Outcomes survive restart and later edits/deletion/schema changes. A missing lookup does not prove an in-flight command failed. There is no automatic retry or expiry, and other mutation types remain outside this changeset-only ledger. The database backup preserves operational outcomes; project JSON export excludes them. Architecture and developer guidance own contracts and recovery examples.

Regression checks cover commit → lost response → server/repository restart → exact lookup/repeat without duplication, concurrent same/different intent, project isolation, cross-connection contention and explicit recovery, full rollback after inserting an outcome, ordered intermediate results/tombstones, invocation capture and CLI recovery across processes. Existing migration fixtures now remove the new table when reconstructing older formats and reject the next unsupported format.

Verification passed: 446 unit tests, strict types, lint, formatting, production/harness builds, all workbench journeys and final merged-coverage dependency/duplication/complexity gates. The full browser run passed 177 of 178 scenarios; the remaining narrow CSV scenario timed out waiting for its initial Project tools button before any mutation. All four CSV scenarios passed an isolated rerun, including that case. No source workaround, quality threshold or exclusion changed.

fields.excerpt:
## API capability discovery and generated reference

2026-10-19: added typed `GET /api/capabilities` with independent `tracer-http` contract version 1, registry-derived operations/features and limits shared with changeset/HTTP enforcement. Discovery needs no model or storage transaction and preserves origin/project/no-cache guards. The first feature promise is `changeset-command-recovery`. Additive operations/features/response fields retain contract 1; incompatible wire or behavior changes require a new contract version.

Clients can opt into captured `require` settings on construction or call `checkCompatibility` explicitly. Checks verify identity, exact supported version, features, operations and minimum limits before writes; configured clients check before obtaining a session. Pending/failed checks block new writes, stale checks cannot restore readiness, and explicit requirements cannot weaken configured ones. Legacy discovery absence reports client-only `incompatible_api`; invalid/unavailable/cancelled reads retain their read/server errors. Existing clients keep their connection behavior until opting in. No automatic retries or per-write negotiation were added.

Query codecs and write helpers expose request metadata used by `npm run api:reference` to generate `docs/api-reference.md`. The unit suite rejects reference drift. This is an endpoint/request index; nested types and semantic guards retain their existing owners. The architecture and developer reference document usage, version policy, scope and recovery.

Verification passed: 455 unit tests, strict types, lint, formatting, production/harness builds, all workbench journeys and final merged-coverage dependency/duplication/complexity gates. New checks cover empty/model-changed discovery without storage reads, origin/project guards, actual advertised-limit enforcement, incompatible/missing/malformed discovery with zero POSTs, captured requirements, additive extensions and stale-check ordering. After removing duplicate capability type declarations, 18 focused API tests passed against the final source. The full browser run passed 177 of 178 scenarios; the remaining Engineering setup case timed out waiting for the Matrix button after reopening the server. Both desktop/narrow setup cases passed an isolated rerun. No source workaround, quality threshold or exclusion changed.

### ND-01 — begin without an extensive setup detour

> As an author starting a design, I want to work with recognizable information so I can begin expressing the design instead of learning the tool's internal model.

**Needs:** PN-01, PN-02. **Basis:** vision plus hypothesis; preferred onboarding method unknown.

**Candidate acceptance:** users recognize the available information and what is missing; they can start one meaningful item without first constructing a complete project ontology. Existing data brought into the project is not silently lost or falsely represented as validated.

**Investigate:** write from scratch, paste/import or start from a template? Prototype these alternatives rather than implementing all three now.

fields.excerpt:
### ND-02 — author in context and move between levels

> As an author, I want to inspect the relevant parent intent while writing a child requirement so I can explain how the child contributes without repeatedly reconstructing context.

**Needs:** PN-02, PN-03, PN-09. **Basis:** UR-1, UR-2, UR-4.

**Candidate acceptance:** free text is usable without compulsory formal syntax; an item can relate to an existing parent or remain explicitly unlinked; applicable field/relationship actions are reachable in the working context; changing scope does not silently lose the draft.

**Exceptions:** long statements, optional attributes, multiple parents, uncertain relationships and a parent that changed while drafting.

fields.title: ND-02 — author in context and move between levels

fields.excerpt:
### ND-03 — inspect siblings and shared identity

> As an engineer reviewing decomposition, I want to see the other items contributing under the relevant parent so I can judge the family together rather than inspect isolated statements.

**Needs:** PN-03, PN-09. **Basis:** UR-1.

**Candidate acceptance:** the parent and relationship defining the family are explainable; shared children remain recognizable as the same underlying item; editing one identity does not create divergence among its appearances; users can return to the wider scope with drafts intact.

**Exceptions:** a child belongs to two parents, appears along several paths, or has different kinds of sibling relationships. Test whether the user wants immediate siblings or the whole branch; do not assume they are equivalent.
fields.heading: ### ND-03 — inspect siblings and shared identity
fields.title: ND-03 — inspect siblings and shared identity

fields.excerpt:
### ND-04 — resolve one meaningful completeness gap

> As an engineer building a design, I want to know which obligation is unresolved and why so I can choose the next appropriate work.

**Needs:** PN-04, PN-03, PN-07. **Basis:** UR-4, UR-15; exact scope/policies are HY.

**Candidate acceptance:** a displayed gap has an explainable expectation and scope; the user can inspect existing candidates before creating duplicate information; an appropriate new connection resolves that structural gap without falsely declaring the design/evidence valid; other unresolved obligations remain visible.

**Software acceptance example (UR-15):** where the project marks a requirement approved, see whether an actual implementation artifact is linked. With no such link, show implementation as not traced and likely outstanding; offer the task choices of implementing it, linking existing code or investigating uncertainty. Do not force a new implementation when the code already exists. A link to a planned task/design is not an actual-code realization link; partial or outdated mappings retain their unresolved scope. Adding an appropriate link closes the trace gap, not automatically the implementation/verification judgment.

**Exceptions:** an item is intentionally not applicable, the expectation is unknown, existing implementation is unlinked, a link covers only part of the requirement or refers to older behavior, or old evidence uses different inputs. Represent uncertainty rather than inventing a complete/incomplete judgment.

### SC-01 — see impact before accepting a change

> As an engineer proposing a modification, I want to compare it with the established state and inspect explainable consequences so I can review the proposal before changing the authoritative design.

**Needs:** PN-05, PN-03, PN-08. **Basis:** UR-4, UR-6, UR-11; specific staging mechanisms are HY.

**Candidate acceptance:** proposed versus committed information is distinguishable; impact candidates show the paths/reasons that make them relevant; browsing does not write changes; connection alone is not presented as proof that the connected item must change; unmodeled consequences remain explicitly possible.

**Exceptions:** cyclic or dense networks, shared children, changed schema, missing/deleted items and incomplete source knowledge. A bounded result must explain its scope, not imply a complete impact census.

> As an engineer considering removing information, I want to see what relies on it so I can decide how to address those obligations without losing the established history.

**Needs:** PN-05, PN-03, PN-08. **Basis:** UR-4.

**Candidate acceptance:** removing, filtering out, disconnecting and superseding are distinguishable; references and unresolved obligations are explained; no silent cascade; established history remains inspectable; users know whether anything was committed.

**Investigate:** actual review/approval authority and the semantics of retirement versus deletion. Do not introduce automatic cascade or organizational approval merely because it would simplify a mockup.

### SC-03 — reassess evidence without rewriting its past

> As a reviewer, I want to inspect changed inputs and the original evidence so I can record why the evidence does or does not support the decision now.

**Needs:** PN-07, PN-05, PN-08. **Basis:** vision/existing evidence model; detailed reviewer task is HY.

**Candidate acceptance:** coverage, freshness, uncertainty and review decision remain separate; original snapshots/rationale remain accessible; the comparison used while drafting is identifiable; a relevant intervening change requires an explicit new assessment rather than silent token adoption; acceptance does not erase drift.

**Exceptions:** missing observations, unrelated edits, relevant later changes, superseded evidence and conflicting reviewer assumptions. Local provenance labels are not authenticated approval authority.

fields.excerpt:
## 4. Cross-cutting story Q-01 — quantitative meaning without overconstraint

> As an engineer changing an important specification, I want to understand where the value comes from and where it is used so I can assess the consequences without forcing every requirement into a formal model.

**Needs:** PN-06, PN-02, PN-05. **Basis:** UR-5; representation and computation are HY.

**Toy scenario:** an overall timing limit is 100 ms, with explicitly declared 60 ms and 40 ms allocations. Propose changing the total to 80 ms. These are not medical specifications. Any arithmetic requires explicit combination and overhead assumptions.

**Candidate acceptance examples:**

- Free-text-only requirements remain authorable and reviewable.
- If a value is deliberately shared, its confirmed consumers are identifiable; an unrelated identical number is not automatically coupled.
- An explicitly modeled calculation may report a result/violation under its declared assumptions, with units and explanation.
- A parent limit change exposes the allocation question but does not silently proportionally scale or rewrite children.
- A child allocation change can raise a feasibility question for the parent without rewriting the parent's intent.
- Missing derivation knowledge is not represented as a satisfied constraint or no impact.
- Declared constraints, possible engineering impact and review decisions are distinguishable.

**Alternatives to test:** ordinary prose with annotated values, optional named typed values, linked value references, and human-authored derivation explanations. A general formula language or extraction engine is not assumed.

**Additional cases:** inconsistent units, rounding, tolerances, ranges, conditions, repeated values, independent choices and removal of a referenced value. Replace the toy example with one real artifact before specifying storage or arithmetic behavior.

fields.excerpt:
## 5. Cross-cutting story R-01 — resume and recover safely

> As an engineer interrupted during work, I want to retain my proposal and orientation so I can resume or reconcile it without losing information or overwriting someone else's change.

**Needs:** PN-08, PN-09. **Basis:** vision; preferred saving/recovery model is HY.

**Candidate acceptance:** context/selection and save status are understandable; switching level or representation does not silently discard drafts; a failed read cannot authorize editing stale information as if current; object/schema conflicts preserve the attempt; historical inspection does not masquerade as editing current state.

**Investigate:** autosave versus explicit save, reopening after shutdown, undo, and what should be retained across sessions. Prototype and actual repository safety capabilities may differ; label unsupported recovery behavior honestly.

fields.acceptance:
**Candidate acceptance:** a displayed gap has an explainable expectation and scope; the user can inspect existing candidates before creating duplicate information; an appropriate new connection resolves that structural gap without falsely declaring the design/evidence valid; other unresolved obligations remain visible.

**Software acceptance example (UR-15):** where the project marks a requirement approved, see whether an actual implementation artifact is linked. With no such link, show implementation as not traced and likely outstanding; offer the task choices of implementing it, linking existing code or investigating uncertainty. Do not force a new implementation when the code already exists. A link to a planned task/design is not an actual-code realization link; partial or outdated mappings retain their unresolved scope. Adding an appropriate link closes the trace gap, not automatically the implementation/verification judgment.
fields.context: Existing candidate scenario; see captured source for full journey and evidence.
fields.exceptions: **Exceptions:** an item is intentionally not applicable, the expectation is unknown, existing implementation is unlinked, a link covers only part of the requirement or refers to older behavior, or old evidence uses different inputs. Represent uncertainty rather than inventing a complete/incomplete judgment.

fields.acceptance: AC-1: Pinned project-model bindings define requirement, method, case and execution vocabulary against the governing schema; edits, deletion and incompatible schema changes cannot silently reinterpret existing verification. AC-2: Cases retain an exact requirement basis, stable criterion IDs, validated native acceptance text ranges/quotes, complete or explicitly partial source coverage and exact criterion-to-method assignments; missing or duplicate obligations cannot become verified. AC-3: Controlled executions atomically preserve activity identity, exact method/requirement/design/supporting input states, conditions, actual observations and typed per-criterion passed/failed/blocked/not_run results with immutable receipts; prose outcomes and report links alone are insufficient. AC-4: Guarded result selection accounts for selected and competing executions, requires rationale for supersession, rejects unrelated scope and prevents a later unassessed failure or partial run from being silently bypassed in favor of an older passing result. AC-5: Analysis separates planning coverage, execution outcome, evidence drift/unknowns, assessed applicability and effective scoped verification. Full verification requires every declared obligation passed/applicable, complete source coverage and a controlled immutable conclusion; authored status alone cannot establish it. AC-6: Relevant requirement/method/design/support changes preserve historical execution/conclusions and require explicit reassessment or basis revision. Unrelated annotations do not retire applicability; unknown material and stale comparison/proposal guards cannot establish current verification. AC-7: Core, typed HTTP/client and CLI share guarded atomic operations, original-intent success recovery, stable identities and bounded complete reads, including invalid, partial, stale, interrupted, superseded and reopened/reassessed cases in two materially different configured domains. AC-8: A real currently unverified Tracer requirement retains unchanged acceptance and a declared method, genuine failing execution, justified correction, passing verification and later relevant-change reassessment. Original failures/candidates remain inspectable; failures are not manufactured to satisfy this lifecycle. AC-9: The shared workspace authors verification bases/executions/selections and explains results/outstanding work through shared services, retains drafts and uncertain-save recovery, and undergoes an independent fresh-agent task with material findings addressed and human validation explicitly separate. AC-10: Existing identity/history/evidence/outcomes and interface/storage compatibility are preserved, deliberate migrations are rehearsed if needed, deterministic export/SQLite backup recovery is verified, owning docs/register retain exact candidate evidence and uncertainties, and appropriate regression/architecture/quality gates pass unchanged.
fields.remaining: Pinned model resolution and exact native criterion/method basis preparation are implemented and phase-verified across two vocabularies. Controlled case/execution/selection/conclusion operations, full actual/second-domain lifecycle, shared verification UI/fresh-agent comprehension and complete AC-1–10/full-goal acceptance remain pending.

fields.acceptance: AC-1: Pinned project-model bindings define requirement, method, case and execution vocabulary against the governing schema; edits, deletion and incompatible schema changes cannot silently reinterpret existing verification. AC-2: Cases retain an exact requirement basis, stable criterion IDs, validated native acceptance text ranges/quotes, complete or explicitly partial source coverage and exact criterion-to-method assignments; missing or duplicate obligations cannot become verified. AC-3: Controlled executions atomically preserve activity identity, exact method/requirement/design/supporting input states, conditions, actual observations and typed per-criterion passed/failed/blocked/not_run results with immutable receipts; prose outcomes and report links alone are insufficient. AC-4: Guarded result selection accounts for selected and competing executions, requires rationale for supersession, rejects unrelated scope and prevents a later unassessed failure or partial run from being silently bypassed in favor of an older passing result. AC-5: Analysis separates planning coverage, execution outcome, evidence drift/unknowns, assessed applicability and effective scoped verification. Full verification requires every declared obligation passed/applicable, complete source coverage and a controlled immutable conclusion; authored status alone cannot establish it. AC-6: Relevant requirement/method/design/support changes preserve historical execution/conclusions and require explicit reassessment or basis revision. Unrelated annotations do not retire applicability; unknown material and stale comparison/proposal guards cannot establish current verification. AC-7: Core, typed HTTP/client and CLI share guarded atomic operations, original-intent success recovery, stable identities and bounded complete reads, including invalid, partial, stale, interrupted, superseded and reopened/reassessed cases in two materially different configured domains. AC-8: A real currently unverified Tracer requirement retains unchanged acceptance and a declared method, genuine failing execution, justified correction, passing verification and later relevant-change reassessment. Original failures/candidates remain inspectable; failures are not manufactured to satisfy this lifecycle. AC-9: The shared workspace authors verification bases/executions/selections and explains results/outstanding work through shared services, retains drafts and uncertain-save recovery, and undergoes an independent fresh-agent task with material findings addressed and human validation explicitly separate. AC-10: Existing identity/history/evidence/outcomes and interface/storage compatibility are preserved, deliberate migrations are rehearsed if needed, deterministic export/SQLite backup recovery is verified, owning docs/register retain exact candidate evidence and uncertainties, and appropriate regression/architecture/quality gates pass unchanged.

fields.acceptance: AC-1: Controlled capture retains an explicit bounded set of exact native member/relationship revisions, external observation selections, schema/context and declared scope; omissions and legacy captures never imply undeclared topology/content completeness. Stable caller identity and captured original intent recover an identical committed capture after lost response/restart without duplicate creation or silent rebasing; conflicting intent/guards/provenance reject. AC-2: A deterministic read-only comparison binds two immutable configuration identities and all governing policy/state digests. Later live native/evidence changes do not alter that pair comparison; switching either side is explicit. Incompatible subject/project/model/schema/scope and unavailable historical information produce explained comparability/uncertainty or refusal rather than inferred equivalence. AC-3: Native comparison explains added/removed membership, type/key/resource/field differences and version-only changes with exact original/current-selected versions, schemas and provenance. Missing versus null, ordered arrays and nested JSON remain meaningful. Removed-from-configuration is distinct from deleted-from-project, and mutable current liveness is not silently substituted for the selected state. AC-4: Selected relationship topology comparison preserves exact endpoints, type, metadata and contextual-reference role/selector/state changes, including relinking, removed relationships and historical endpoints. Undeclared legacy topology is explicitly unknown, not an empty complete graph; no reachability implies engineering causation or membership. AC-5: Content comparison uses explicitly captured resource/observation identities, availability and hashes/commits; annotation changes and observed-byte changes remain separate. Same hash is not identity merging or byte retention, and document change cannot establish passage change without sufficient selected evidence. Reads perform no observer IO and never replace pinned selections with the latest observation. AC-6: Configuration-bound dependency/applicability analysis explains changed inputs, potentially affected and unaffected declared scope, exact inclusion/exclusion basis and remaining uncertainty. Captured input field/path/direct-link/content semantics are reused; incomplete scope, absent evidence and unknown availability cannot establish no impact. Bounded populations and summaries state completeness and refuse overflow explicitly. AC-7: Controlled pair-bound assessments preserve the original pair/policy and every discovered obligation, reasoned disposition, action and immutable conclusion. No-action, investigation, required revision and re-verification remain distinct. Pair/policy changes require explicit reassessment while retaining prior judgments; closure requires complete accounting under the pinned policy and never implies release approval. AC-8: Verification follow-through retains exact criterion/method/candidate/support states and explains whether selected recorded outcomes apply to the target configuration, independently of unrelated live-head changes. Existing current-head verification keeps its meaning. Failed/not_run results stay non-passing; generic reviews/status strings cannot override changed governing criteria, incomplete accounting or unknown support. Work executed after configuration capture can support that candidate only through validated exact input correspondence and explicit provenance, never by silently adding membership. AC-9: Core, typed HTTP/client and CLI/agent interfaces share the same domain operations, captured queries and original-intent recovery. Atomic guards reject stale/concurrent/invalid proposals without partial state/history/evidence/outcomes; failed reads pause writes and uncertain writes are inspected without automatic replay. Existing API/storage/receipt/configuration/baseline/assessment/verification contracts retain their semantics and historical readability. AC-10: The shared workspace captures/selects the pair, explains native/content/topology differences and comparable/unknown scope, investigates consequences, records dispositions, opens appropriate existing assessment/verification follow-through and shows outstanding/resolved work. Drafts survive navigation, stale inputs require explicit adoption, lost responses use shared recovery and supported responsive views preserve exact context. A fresh independent agent completes an unfamiliar task and material findings are addressed; human validation remains separate. AC-11: A justified real Tracer software change retains exact before/after configurations and original conclusions, identifies actual changed and unaffected scope, completes necessary assessment/verification and explains final remaining work without manufactured engineering claims. A materially different configured domain demonstrates the same semantics. Exact candidate/procedure/results cover additions/removals, reference/content changes, unavailable/deleted inputs, partial/incompatible scope, drift, supersession/reassessment and workload/payload boundaries. AC-12: Existing identities, native/evidence history, command outcomes and both prior application capabilities are preserved; necessary migrations are rehearsed and deterministic export/online SQLite backup/restored recovery verified. Appropriate regression, browser, architecture and quality gates pass unchanged. Owning architecture/usage docs, checkpoint and register retain exact evidence, unchanged criteria, delivery/verification/human-validation distinctions and remaining limits. Full goal acceptance is audited before completion.
